faqs.question: Can I use Amla for both hair and skin?
faqs.answer: Yes. Choose a hair-conditioning mask or a simple rinse-off skin routine and follow the separate directions on the pack. Test on a small area first, and do not use hair-mask timing on the face.

faqs.question: Can I mix Amla with Hibiscus?
faqs.answer: They can be used in a hair-mask routine after you have tried each separately. Start skin care with one powder and water so you can judge how your skin responds.

faqs.question: Does Ayurvedic use mean the benefits are clinically proven?
faqs.answer: No. Ayurvedic tradition and clinical product testing are different. Amla research on extracts or oral preparations does not prove the same effects from this cosmetic powder.

description:
Bring Amla into the part of your routine that needs a little time and care. This fruit powder is a versatile ingredient for conditioning hair masks and simple rinse-off face masks.

For hair, use it in a pre-wash routine for a softer feel and natural-looking shine. For skin, keep the preparation simple, apply without scrubbing and follow the skin-use directions on the pack. Introduce one botanical at a time.

Amla has a place in Ayurvedic tradition. Ingredient research does not establish clinical results for this powder; this is cosmetic care, not a treatment for hair loss or skin conditions.

faqs.question: Will Indigo alone make grey hair black?
faqs.answer: Not reliably. It can look blue or green on light or grey hair. Darker-looking results usually involve a planned henna-and-indigo process, and individual results vary.

faqs.question: Can Indigo be used for skin care?
faqs.answer: No. This product is for scalp-hair colouring only. Do not apply it as a face mask or use it on eyebrows or eyelashes.

faqs.question: Why do I need both a skin test and a strand test?
faqs.answer: The skin test checks for a possible reaction according to the pack instructions, while the strand test previews the shade on your hair. Neither test should be skipped, and a clear skin test cannot guarantee that no reaction will occur.

description:
Indigo leaf powder is selected for one clear purpose: plant-based hair colour. It is commonly used in a planned henna-and-indigo routine to develop darker-looking shades.

The result depends on your starting colour, porosity, previous treatments and preparation. Indigo alone can appear blue or green on light or grey hair; it does not reliably turn grey hair black by itself.

Follow the full pack instructions, carry out the directed skin test before every use and test a strand before colouring all your hair. Indigo is for scalp hair only, not skin-care masks, eyebrows or eyelashes.
